articles.title: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant teams win three gold awards at international quality convention in Dhaka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: All three Quality Control Circle teams from RINL win the top honour at ICQCC-2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, has secured three Gold Awards at the International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026) hosted by the Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) in Dhaka from November 18 to 20. Participating in the hybrid-mode convention, three Quality Control Circle teams from the steel plant presented their technical case studies online from the Centre for HRD at Ukku House on November 19, with all three entries clinching the top honour. Team ‘AMPS’ from the Blast Furnace department, comprising M.V. Ramana, P. Sai Narendra Kumar, Ahammad Valli, P.M. Satyanarayana and K. Suresh, won the award for their project on modifying the vacuum contactor of the HT motor in the slag granulation plant. From SMS-1, team ‘SAAPHALYA’, represented by G. Siva Sankar Rao, Bhanu Kiran Banda, G. Appa Rao and P. Simhachalam, earned gold for their case study on LD converter ID fan lubrication oil pipeline modification. Team ‘UNNATI’ from the Utilities department, consisting of Niranjan Shailendra, Bhavani Ramyasree Utala, Sugunavathi Seepana and K. Srinivasa Rao, bagged the third gold for devising an innovative method to synchronise a high-pressure 4.5 MW nitrogen compressor motor.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The RINL management congratulated the winning teams, noting that the international recognition reflected the workforce’s technical competence, teamwork and commitment to operational excellence.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Visakhapatnam Steel Plant teams win three gold awards at international quality convention in Dhaka

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:50:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: All three Quality Control Circle teams from RINL win the top honour at ICQCC-2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, has secured three Gold Awards at the International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026) hosted by the Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) in Dhaka from November 18 to 20. Participating in the hybrid-mode convention, three Quality Control Circle teams from the steel plant presented their technical case studies online from the Centre for HRD at Ukku House on November 19, with all three entries clinching the top honour. Team ‘AMPS’ from the Blast Furnace department, comprising M.V. Ramana, P. Sai Narendra Kumar, Ahammad Valli, P.M. Satyanarayana and K. Suresh, won the award for their project on modifying the vacuum contactor of the HT motor in the slag granulation plant. From SMS-1, team ‘SAAPHALYA’, represented by G. Siva Sankar Rao, Bhanu Kiran Banda, G. Appa Rao and P. Simhachalam, earned gold for their case study on LD converter ID fan lubrication oil pipeline modification. Team ‘UNNATI’ from the Utilities department, consisting of Niranjan Shailendra, Bhavani Ramyasree Utala, Sugunavathi Seepana and K. Srinivasa Rao, bagged the third gold for devising an innovative method to synchronise a high-pressure 4.5 MW nitrogen compressor motor.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The RINL management congratulated the winning teams, noting that the international recognition reflected the workforce’s technical competence, teamwork and commitment to operational excellence.

दानेदार बनाने का कार्य — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Granulation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:48:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Cooperative (Adjective)
को-ऑपरेटिव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Cooperative' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Alienation (Noun)
अलगाव की भावना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Alienation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare." (Hinglish Arth: इस वर्ष अट्टापडी में बार-बार होने वाली शिशु मृत्यु एक ऐसे संकट की ओर इशारा करती है जो कुपोषण और समय पर स्वास्थ्य देखभाल तक पहुंच से परे है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care." (Hinglish Arth: ग्राउंड ज़ीरो/केरलम/शिशु/स्वास्थ्य/सरकारी स्वास्थ्य देखभाल)

articles.title: ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: PM Modi, referring to the fall in prices of gold, said, ‘A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) expressed happiness over people buying less gold following an appeal made by him last year, claiming gold prices fell due to this. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, Mr. Modi said, "Today, you must have seen that there is a lot of discussion in the media and on social media. In that discussion, everyone is saying today that Modi ji said in Parliament in 2023 that you should invest your money in bonds issued by the Government of India's PSUs. You will make a fortune. People mocked me at the time, but today history bears witness that those who invested made a fortune." Referring to the fall in prices of gold, Mr. Modi said, "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it, and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell." He went on to say, "Today, I'm going to say something else. Mark my words: Times are changing, and people with skills will be valued more than those who go around with paper certificates, wearing suits and ties. Demand for those with skills, those with talent, will increase."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PM further said, "I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji’s request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation."

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:48:51 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: PM Modi, referring to the fall in prices of gold, said, ‘A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) expressed happiness over people buying less gold following an appeal made by him last year, claiming gold prices fell due to this. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, Mr. Modi said, "Today, you must have seen that there is a lot of discussion in the media and on social media. In that discussion, everyone is saying today that Modi ji said in Parliament in 2023 that you should invest your money in bonds issued by the Government of India's PSUs. You will make a fortune. People mocked me at the time, but today history bears witness that those who invested made a fortune." Referring to the fall in prices of gold, Mr. Modi said, "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it, and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell." He went on to say, "Today, I'm going to say something else. Mark my words: Times are changing, and people with skills will be valued more than those who go around with paper certificates, wearing suits and ties. Demand for those with skills, those with talent, will increase."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PM further said, "I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji’s request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation."

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Convocation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Parliament (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Parliament' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Certificates (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Certificates' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. PM Modi, referring to the fall in prices of gold, said, ‘A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of '‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi rec' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to '‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that '‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "PM Modi, referring to the fall in prices of gold, said, ‘A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold..." (Hinglish Arth: पीएम मोदी ने सोने की कीमतों में गिरावट का जिक्र करते हुए कहा, 'एक साल पहले मैंने अपने देशवासियों से आग्रह किया था कि अगर उन्हें जरूरत नहीं है तो कृपया एक साल तक सोना न खरीदें.')
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Such is the character of this nation.".
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Such is the character of this nation."." (Hinglish Arth: इस राष्ट्र का चरित्र ही ऐसा है।”)

articles.title: Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practice successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 05:18:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practice successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Helmetless riding cases in Bengaluru more than double compared to 2025, touch 42.90 lakh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A senior BTP officer told The Hindu that the number of cases had doubled because violations had been booked with zero tolerance through contactless enforcement over the last five months

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A whopping 42.90 lakh challans were issued for riding without a helmet in Bengaluru in the first 10 months of 2026, more than double the 20.22 lakh cases booked in the whole of 2025. Data from the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP), reviewed by The Hindu in the wake of a helmetless rider dying in a road accident recently, showed that cases of riding without a helmet increased by 112.47% in 2026 compared with the total number of cases booked in 2025. However, cases in 2025 had dropped by 25% from 2024 as the year saw only contactless enforcement. Last week, a 19-year-old degree student was killed and an 18-year-old boy sustained severe head injuries after their two-wheeler crashed into a divider on Santhanur Road, North Bengaluru. Neither of them was wearing a helmet. The data also shows that cases of pillion riders travelling without helmets have doubled, with the BTP issuing 26.22 lakh challans for the violation this year, compared with 11.27 lakh in the whole of last year. These two violations continue to be among the traffic rules most frequently flouted by Bengaluru commuters, the data shows. Wrong parking, driving without a seat belt, jumping signals and driving or riding on the wrong side are among the other common violations. A senior BTP officer told The Hindu that the number of cases had doubled because helmetless riding violations had been booked with zero tolerance through contactless enforcement over the last five months. “Helmetless riding has become rampant in the city, and there is an immediate need to curb these cases. Contact enforcement for riding without a helmet has also been increased. However, to curb this violation, we have aggressively started issuing challans from our camera feeds,” the officer said. The increased use of contactless enforcement for booking riding-without-helmet cases is also reflected in the data. In the first three months of 2026, the share of contactless challans dropped from 96% in the corresponding period last year to 84%. In the subsequent months, contactless bookings increased to 90%, and by October, the share had risen to over 92% this year. Another BTP official said curbing helmetless riding would not be possible unless fines were increased. “The Transport Department is exploring legal ways to increase fines for riding on footpaths, which is necessary. Similarly, riding without a helmet should also attract hefty penalties,” the officer said, adding that otherwise, shaping commuter behaviour would be difficult.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The officer further said that, along with increasing penalties, the State government should also stop frequently introducing a 50% concession on traffic challans. Such concessions make it difficult to bring about a change in commuter behaviour.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Helmetless riding cases in Bengaluru more than double compared to 2025, touch 42.90 lakh

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:27:07 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A senior BTP officer told The Hindu that the number of cases had doubled because violations had been booked with zero tolerance through contactless enforcement over the last five months

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A whopping 42.90 lakh challans were issued for riding without a helmet in Bengaluru in the first 10 months of 2026, more than double the 20.22 lakh cases booked in the whole of 2025. Data from the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP), reviewed by The Hindu in the wake of a helmetless rider dying in a road accident recently, showed that cases of riding without a helmet increased by 112.47% in 2026 compared with the total number of cases booked in 2025. However, cases in 2025 had dropped by 25% from 2024 as the year saw only contactless enforcement. Last week, a 19-year-old degree student was killed and an 18-year-old boy sustained severe head injuries after their two-wheeler crashed into a divider on Santhanur Road, North Bengaluru. Neither of them was wearing a helmet. The data also shows that cases of pillion riders travelling without helmets have doubled, with the BTP issuing 26.22 lakh challans for the violation this year, compared with 11.27 lakh in the whole of last year. These two violations continue to be among the traffic rules most frequently flouted by Bengaluru commuters, the data shows. Wrong parking, driving without a seat belt, jumping signals and driving or riding on the wrong side are among the other common violations. A senior BTP officer told The Hindu that the number of cases had doubled because helmetless riding violations had been booked with zero tolerance through contactless enforcement over the last five months. “Helmetless riding has become rampant in the city, and there is an immediate need to curb these cases. Contact enforcement for riding without a helmet has also been increased. However, to curb this violation, we have aggressively started issuing challans from our camera feeds,” the officer said. The increased use of contactless enforcement for booking riding-without-helmet cases is also reflected in the data. In the first three months of 2026, the share of contactless challans dropped from 96% in the corresponding period last year to 84%. In the subsequent months, contactless bookings increased to 90%, and by October, the share had risen to over 92% this year. Another BTP official said curbing helmetless riding would not be possible unless fines were increased. “The Transport Department is exploring legal ways to increase fines for riding on footpaths, which is necessary. Similarly, riding without a helmet should also attract hefty penalties,” the officer said, adding that otherwise, shaping commuter behaviour would be difficult.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The officer further said that, along with increasing penalties, the State government should also stop frequently introducing a 50% concession on traffic challans. Such concessions make it difficult to bring about a change in commuter behaviour.

Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।

सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: A senior BTP officer told The Hindu that the number of cases had doubled because violations had been booked with zero tolerance through contactless enforcement over the last five months
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: A senior BTP officer told The Hindu that the number of cases had doubled because violations had been booked with zero tolerance through contactless enforcement over the last five months
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A whopping 42.90 lakh challans were issued for riding without a helmet in Bengaluru in the first 10 months of 2026, more than double the 20.22 lakh cases booked in the whole of 2025. Data from the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP), reviewed by The Hindu in the wake of a helmetless rider dying in a road accident recently, showed that cases of riding without a helmet increased by 112.47% in 2026 compared with the total number of cases booked in 2025. However, cases in 2025 had dropped by 25% from 2024 as the year saw only contactless enforcement. Last week, a 19-year-old degree student was killed and an 18-year-old boy sustained severe head injuries after their two-wheeler crashed into a divider on Santhanur Road, North Bengaluru. Neither of them was wearing a helmet. The data also shows that cases of pillion riders travelling without helmets have doubled, with the BTP issuing 26.22 lakh challans for the violation this year, compared with 11.27 lakh in the whole of last year. These two violations continue to be among the traffic rules most frequently flouted by Bengaluru commuters, the data shows. Wrong parking, driving without a seat belt, jumping signals and driving or riding on the wrong side are among the other common violations. A senior BTP officer told The Hindu that the number of cases had doubled because helmetless riding violations had been booked with zero tolerance through contactless enforcement over the last five months. “Helmetless riding has become rampant in the city, and there is an immediate need to curb these cases. Contact enforcement for riding without a helmet has also been increased. However, to curb this violation, we have aggressively started issuing challans from our camera feeds,” the officer said. The increased use of contactless enforcement for booking riding-without-helmet cases is also reflected in the data. In the first three months of 2026, the share of contactless challans dropped from 96% in the corresponding period last year to 84%. In the subsequent months, contactless bookings increased to 90%, and by October, the share had risen to over 92% this year. Another BTP official said curbing helmetless riding would not be possible unless fines were increased. “The Transport Department is exploring legal ways to increase fines for riding on footpaths, which is necessary. Similarly, riding without a helmet should also attract hefty penalties,” the officer said, adding that otherwise, shaping commuter behaviour would be difficult.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The officer further said that, along with increasing penalties, the State government should also stop frequently introducing a 50% concession on traffic challans. Such concessions make it difficult to bring about a change in commuter behaviour.

articles.title: Specialised training on the anvil for college teachers, staff in Calicut varsity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Proposals form part of the ASCENT project planned to mark the institution’s diamond jubilee; the university’s Syndicate is expected to consider them soon

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The University of Calicut is planning to organise specialised training programmes for teachers and staff in its affiliated colleges at foundational and advanced levels. A curriculum that incorporates interdisciplinary approaches is in the pipeline too. According to university sources, this is part of the ASCENT (Advancing Standards for College Empowerment and Transformation) project being planned to mark the diamond jubilee of the institution. The university’s Syndicate is expected to consider the proposals soon. The sources say that the training will be provided in areas such as enhancing the operational excellence of colleges, digital office management, securing research grants, and improving the rankings by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) and the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF). A university official says that a special mechanism has been proposed to prepare colleges that have not yet received NAAC or NIRF accreditation or rankings. A transparent digital rating system based on NAAC and NIRF criteria is likely to be introduced to enable the assessment of the academic standards of colleges and the monitoring of their progress. There is plan to introduce certificate and diploma courses in collaboration with recognised industrial establishments alongside regular degree programmes. The objective is to ensure that the students acquire additional skills and become job-ready in fields such as Artificial Intelligence, fintech, and digital media. The project also includes an institutional enterprise resource planning system being developed by the Calicut University Computer Centre. This software, which digitises academic and administrative processes ranging from admissions to the recording of marks, will be made available to colleges at an affordable rate.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A premium tri-monthly publication is also proposed to be launched under the public relations wing to introduce the achievements of the university and its affiliated colleges at the national and international levels. The sources say that the ASCENT project is envisioned to make the colleges active participants in the development process. The proposal were prepared by a team led by the Vice-Chancellor, pro-Vice-Chancellor, and the Director of the College Development Council.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Specialised training on the anvil for college teachers, staff in Calicut varsity

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:24:40 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Proposals form part of the ASCENT project planned to mark the institution’s diamond jubilee; the university’s Syndicate is expected to consider them soon

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The University of Calicut is planning to organise specialised training programmes for teachers and staff in its affiliated colleges at foundational and advanced levels. A curriculum that incorporates interdisciplinary approaches is in the pipeline too. According to university sources, this is part of the ASCENT (Advancing Standards for College Empowerment and Transformation) project being planned to mark the diamond jubilee of the institution. The university’s Syndicate is expected to consider the proposals soon. The sources say that the training will be provided in areas such as enhancing the operational excellence of colleges, digital office management, securing research grants, and improving the rankings by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) and the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF). A university official says that a special mechanism has been proposed to prepare colleges that have not yet received NAAC or NIRF accreditation or rankings. A transparent digital rating system based on NAAC and NIRF criteria is likely to be introduced to enable the assessment of the academic standards of colleges and the monitoring of their progress. There is plan to introduce certificate and diploma courses in collaboration with recognised industrial establishments alongside regular degree programmes. The objective is to ensure that the students acquire additional skills and become job-ready in fields such as Artificial Intelligence, fintech, and digital media. The project also includes an institutional enterprise resource planning system being developed by the Calicut University Computer Centre. This software, which digitises academic and administrative processes ranging from admissions to the recording of marks, will be made available to colleges at an affordable rate.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A premium tri-monthly publication is also proposed to be launched under the public relations wing to introduce the achievements of the university and its affiliated colleges at the national and international levels. The sources say that the ASCENT project is envisioned to make the colleges active participants in the development process. The proposal were prepared by a team led by the Vice-Chancellor, pro-Vice-Chancellor, and the Director of the College Development Council.

Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Transformation (Noun)
परिवर्तन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Transformation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Administrative (Adjective)
प्रशासनिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administrative' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Accreditation (Noun)
प्रत्यायन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Accreditation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

A. Proposals form part of the ASCENT project planned to mark the institution’s diamond jubilee; the university’s Syndicate is expected to consider them...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Specialised training on the anvil for college te' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Specialised training on the anvil for college' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Specialised training on the anvil for college' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Proposals form part of the ASCENT project planned to mark the institution’s diamond jubilee; the university’s Syndicate is expected to consider them..." fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH) hosted the third edition of its half marathon, with about 3,500 participants taking part in it from multiple cities, on Sunday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The event featured four categories including 21.1 km half marathon, 10 km timed run, 5 km timed run and 5 km fun run, and saw students, faculty, alumni, professionals, families and fitness enthusiasts in participation. In the half marathon category, Ramavath Ramesh Chandra who clocked 1hr:16 mins, won the men’s title, and Sunima Dila claimed the women’s title with her timing of 1hr:42 mins. Top finishers in the 10 km-run were Vangala Dhanush and Kodavath Swapna. The race was flagged off by India’s first paralympic gold medallist, Murlikant Rajaram Petkar. “Running teaches us discipline, determination and the ability to push beyond our perceived limits. I encourage young people and working professionals to make physical activity a regular part of their lives. It is heartening to see an institution like IIT Hyderabad, which is at the forefront of research and innovation, also bringing together such a large community through sports,” Mr. Petkar stated, according to a media release.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: IITH Director B. S. Murty said the event reflected the institute’s commitment to promoting physical well-being alongside academic and research excellence.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 About 3,500 runners participate in IITH half marathon 2026

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:24:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH) hosted the third edition of its half marathon, with about 3,500 participants taking part in it from multiple cities, on Sunday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The event featured four categories including 21.1 km half marathon, 10 km timed run, 5 km timed run and 5 km fun run, and saw students, faculty, alumni, professionals, families and fitness enthusiasts in participation. In the half marathon category, Ramavath Ramesh Chandra who clocked 1hr:16 mins, won the men’s title, and Sunima Dila claimed the women’s title with her timing of 1hr:42 mins. Top finishers in the 10 km-run were Vangala Dhanush and Kodavath Swapna. The race was flagged off by India’s first paralympic gold medallist, Murlikant Rajaram Petkar. “Running teaches us discipline, determination and the ability to push beyond our perceived limits. I encourage young people and working professionals to make physical activity a regular part of their lives. It is heartening to see an institution like IIT Hyderabad, which is at the forefront of research and innovation, also bringing together such a large community through sports,” Mr. Petkar stated, according to a media release.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: IITH Director B. S. Murty said the event reflected the institute’s commitment to promoting physical well-being alongside academic and research excellence.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Participation (Noun)
भाग लेना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Participation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Determination (Adjective / Verb)
दृढ़ निश्चय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Determination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Paralympic (Adjective)
पैरालम्पिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Paralympic' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "About 3,500 runners participate in IITH half marathon 2026", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH) hosted the third edition of its half marathon, with about 3,500 participants taking part in it...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'About 3,500 runners participate in IITH half mar' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'About 3,500 runners participate in IITH half ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'About 3,500 runners participate in IITH half ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH) hosted the third edition of its half marathon, with about 3,500 participants taking part in it..." (Hinglish Arth: भारतीय प्रौद्योगिकी संस्थान हैदराबाद (आईआईटीएच) ने रविवार को अपने हाफ मैराथन के तीसरे संस्करण की मेजबानी की, जिसमें कई शहरों से लगभग 3,500 प्रतिभागियों ने भाग लिया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "About 3,500 runners participate in IITH half marathon 2026"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Murty said the event reflected the institute’s commitment to promoting physical well-being alongside academic and research excellence.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Murty said the event reflected the institute’s commitment to promoting physical well-being alongside academic and research excellence." (Hinglish Arth: मूर्ति ने कहा कि यह आयोजन शैक्षणिक और अनुसंधान उत्कृष्टता के साथ-साथ शारीरिक कल्याण को बढ़ावा देने के लिए संस्थान की प्रतिबद्धता को दर्शाता है।)

articles.title: Federation of Islamic Organisations and Political Parties welcomes T.N. govt.’s review petition in Thirupparankundram case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Federation of Islamic Organisations and Political Parties on Sunday welcomed the Tamil Nadu government’s decision to file a review petition in the Supreme Court against its interim order on November 20 that allowed lighting of the lamp at the deepathoon on Karthigai Deepam day as an one time arrangement.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Federation held a meeting in Chennai on Sunday to discuss further course of action in the Thirupparankundram issue. Sources said during the meeting, the Federation urged the Tamil Nadu government to ensure that usual practice of lighting the lamp should be followed this year too, and that permission should be granted only to light it at the customary spot near the Uchchi Pillaiyar temple.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Federation also said the Tamil Nadu government has a responsibility to protect communal harmony in the Thirupparankundram issue. It urged the government to engage senior advocates to argue the case and ensure the long-standing practice of lighting the lamp was continued.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Federation of Islamic Organisations and Political Parties welcomes T.N. govt.’s review petition in Thirupparankundram case

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:24:15 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Federation of Islamic Organisations and Political Parties on Sunday welcomed the Tamil Nadu government’s decision to file a review petition in the Supreme Court against its interim order on November 20 that allowed lighting of the lamp at the deepathoon on Karthigai Deepam day as an one time arrangement.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Federation held a meeting in Chennai on Sunday to discuss further course of action in the Thirupparankundram issue. Sources said during the meeting, the Federation urged the Tamil Nadu government to ensure that usual practice of lighting the lamp should be followed this year too, and that permission should be granted only to light it at the customary spot near the Uchchi Pillaiyar temple.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Federation also said the Tamil Nadu government has a responsibility to protect communal harmony in the Thirupparankundram issue. It urged the government to engage senior advocates to argue the case and ensure the long-standing practice of lighting the lamp was continued.

articles.title: BJP targets Congress after traders’ body thanks PM Modi for cautionary advice on buying gold
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Chamber of Trade and Industry says the PM Modi’s advice had saved lakhs of jewellers, traders, and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) targeted the Congress after a traders’ body thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his advice earlier this year to postpone gold purchases. “When PM @narendramodi appealed to the people of India to defer the purchase of gold, Congress called it a ‘death warrant’. With gold prices falling globally, traders who followed PM Modi’s advice saved ₹65 lakh per kg of gold! The traders’ body has thanked the Prime Minister today!” BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said. “The Gandhi-Vadra family, which lived a lavish lifestyle when the majority of India’s population was poor, should take a master class in economic management and simple living from PM Modi,” Mr. Bhandari said in a post on social media platform X, demanding that the Congress apologise to traders for “misleading them and creating panic”. His remarks came after the Chamber of Trade and Industry wrote to Mr. Modi, thanking him for his advice to people in May 2026 against purchasing gold. The group said the advice saved lakhs of jewellers, traders, and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell from ₹1.90 crore to ₹1.25 crore, a decline of ₹65 lakh per kg. The dip in gold prices had brought relief to families during the ongoing wedding season, it said. In another post, Mr. Bhandari cited data to stress that India’s economic transformation under Mr. Modi had been “phenomenal”. He said the country’s GDP was $1.86 trillion in 2013, while it rose to $4.1 trillion in 2026; forex reserves increased from $295 billion to $690 billion; exports from $450 billion to $825 billion; manufacturing output from $280 billion to $500 billion; and defence exports from ₹686 crore to ₹38,622 crore.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The BJP leader said salaried employment had expanded, with the number of women in salaried employment rising from one crore to four crores.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 BJP targets Congress after traders’ body thanks PM Modi for cautionary advice on buying gold

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:24:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Chamber of Trade and Industry says the PM Modi’s advice had saved lakhs of jewellers, traders, and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) targeted the Congress after a traders’ body thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his advice earlier this year to postpone gold purchases. “When PM @narendramodi appealed to the people of India to defer the purchase of gold, Congress called it a ‘death warrant’. With gold prices falling globally, traders who followed PM Modi’s advice saved ₹65 lakh per kg of gold! The traders’ body has thanked the Prime Minister today!” BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said. “The Gandhi-Vadra family, which lived a lavish lifestyle when the majority of India’s population was poor, should take a master class in economic management and simple living from PM Modi,” Mr. Bhandari said in a post on social media platform X, demanding that the Congress apologise to traders for “misleading them and creating panic”. His remarks came after the Chamber of Trade and Industry wrote to Mr. Modi, thanking him for his advice to people in May 2026 against purchasing gold. The group said the advice saved lakhs of jewellers, traders, and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell from ₹1.90 crore to ₹1.25 crore, a decline of ₹65 lakh per kg. The dip in gold prices had brought relief to families during the ongoing wedding season, it said. In another post, Mr. Bhandari cited data to stress that India’s economic transformation under Mr. Modi had been “phenomenal”. He said the country’s GDP was $1.86 trillion in 2013, while it rose to $4.1 trillion in 2026; forex reserves increased from $295 billion to $690 billion; exports from $450 billion to $825 billion; manufacturing output from $280 billion to $500 billion; and defence exports from ₹686 crore to ₹38,622 crore.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The BJP leader said salaried employment had expanded, with the number of women in salaried employment rising from one crore to four crores.

प्रबंध — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Management' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Phenomenal (Adjective)
अभूतपूर्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Phenomenal' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "BJP targets Congress after traders’ body thanks PM Modi for cautionary advice on buying gold", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Chamber of Trade and Industry says the PM Modi’s advice had saved lakhs of jewellers, traders, and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'BJP targets Congress after traders’ body thanks ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'BJP targets Congress after traders’ body than' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'BJP targets Congress after traders’ body than' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Chamber of Trade and Industry says the PM Modi’s advice had saved lakhs of jewellers, traders, and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "BJP targets Congress after traders’ body thanks PM Modi for cautionary advice on buying gold"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The BJP leader said salaried employment had expanded, with the number of women in salaried employment rising from one crore to four crores.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The BJP leader said salaried employment had expanded, with the number of women in salaried employment rising from one crore to four crores." (Hinglish Arth: भाजपा नेता ने कहा कि वेतनभोगी रोजगार का विस्तार हुआ है, वेतनभोगी रोजगार में महिलाओं की संख्या एक करोड़ से बढ़कर चार करोड़ हो गई है।)

articles.title: Myanmar calls ASEAN review of peace plan 'unfair and imbalanced'; questions bloc's treatment
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila did not reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar has termed the ASEAN leaders' assessment of its implementation of a five-point peace plan "unfair and imbalanced", accusing the regional bloc of disregarding its views and denying it equal rights and representation as a member state. In a statement issued on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila on November 15, 2026 did not adequately reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country. "Although ASEAN has yet to reach a consensus, Myanmar continues to engage bilaterally with individual ASEAN Member states," the Ministry said, expressing appreciation to members that had extended support and assistance in recognition of what it described as positive developments in the country. The statement comes after ASEAN leaders reiterated their concern over insufficient progress in implementing the five-point peace plan agreed upon in April 2021 following the military takeover in Myanmar. They also extended restrictions on the country's leadership attending the bloc's summits, saying the ban would remain until there was meaningful progress in implementing the plan. Under the arrangement, Myanmar can be represented at ASEAN summits only by a non-political representative, such as a career diplomat. The five-point consensus calls for an immediate cessation of violence, dialogue among all parties, an ASEAN special envoy to facilitate mediation, a visit by the envoy to Myanmar to meet all parties, and humanitarian assistance through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management. The conflict in Myanmar has continued since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, triggering widespread protests, a military crackdown and an armed resistance movement. ASEAN's five-point consensus was adopted in April 2021 in an attempt to end the violence and facilitate a peaceful resolution to the crisis. However, the bloc has repeatedly expressed frustration over the lack of progress in its implementation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rejecting criticism of its handling of the conflict, Myanmar said it had continued to cooperate with ASEAN's suggestions and recommendations while safeguarding its national interests and sovereignty.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Myanmar calls ASEAN review of peace plan 'unfair and imbalanced'; questions bloc's treatment

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 06:55:30 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila did not reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar has termed the ASEAN leaders' assessment of its implementation of a five-point peace plan "unfair and imbalanced", accusing the regional bloc of disregarding its views and denying it equal rights and representation as a member state. In a statement issued on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila on November 15, 2026 did not adequately reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country. "Although ASEAN has yet to reach a consensus, Myanmar continues to engage bilaterally with individual ASEAN Member states," the Ministry said, expressing appreciation to members that had extended support and assistance in recognition of what it described as positive developments in the country. The statement comes after ASEAN leaders reiterated their concern over insufficient progress in implementing the five-point peace plan agreed upon in April 2021 following the military takeover in Myanmar. They also extended restrictions on the country's leadership attending the bloc's summits, saying the ban would remain until there was meaningful progress in implementing the plan. Under the arrangement, Myanmar can be represented at ASEAN summits only by a non-political representative, such as a career diplomat. The five-point consensus calls for an immediate cessation of violence, dialogue among all parties, an ASEAN special envoy to facilitate mediation, a visit by the envoy to Myanmar to meet all parties, and humanitarian assistance through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management. The conflict in Myanmar has continued since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, triggering widespread protests, a military crackdown and an armed resistance movement. ASEAN's five-point consensus was adopted in April 2021 in an attempt to end the violence and facilitate a peaceful resolution to the crisis. However, the bloc has repeatedly expressed frustration over the lack of progress in its implementation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rejecting criticism of its handling of the conflict, Myanmar said it had continued to cooperate with ASEAN's suggestions and recommendations while safeguarding its national interests and sovereignty.

Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।

Representation (Noun)
प्रतिनिधित्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Representation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Appreciation (Noun)
प्रशंसा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Appreciation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries other than their own have endured hunger, thirst and other deprivations while being detained indefinitely in places with poor human rights records and little oversight. For those expelled to South Sudan, and their families, the ordeal has come at an additional cost. Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones. Instead, the guards pocketed most of the money, families said, while detainees went for days without food or clean water, and months held incommunicado. “They used our desperate situation,” said Ngoc Phan, a U.S. citizen whose husband Tuan Phan had been detained in South Sudan for nearly a year before he was repatriated to Vietnam in June. “If that's not exploitation, I don't know what is.” It is the inevitable outcome, she said, of a U.S. immigration policy that places deportees in the custody of countries struggling with poverty and corruption, then looks the other way. Five deportees remain in custody in South Sudan, a country in East Africa where millions face severe hunger and poverty after years of civil conflict and devastating floods. The economy is in tatters, and government workers rarely receive wages. In all, Ms. Ngoc Phan said she forked over roughly $4,000 intended for food, water and a cellphone. She sent several hundred dollars on multiple occasions and each time, her husband said, guards would give him a few bananas and apples, and some peanuts. Mr. Tuan Phan, 44, said he lost 20 pounds while under confinement at a gated three-story building in Juba, the capital, and that tensions grew between detainees and guards as living conditions worsened. One detainee who wanted a window open for fresh air was struck in the face by a guard, and another who complained about a lack of soap was locked in his room for days and only let out to eat, he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “I feared for my life every day I was there,” he said.

1. Core Context & Background: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries other than their own have endured hunger, thirst and other deprivations while being detained indefinitely in places with poor human rights records and little oversight. The economy is in tatters, and government workers rarely receive wages. In all, Ms. Ngoc Phan said she forked over roughly $4,000 intended for food, water and a cellphone. She sent several hundred dollars on multiple occasions and each time, her husband said, guards would give him a few bananas and apples, and some peanuts. Mr. Tuan Phan, 44, said he lost 20 pounds while under confinement at a gated three-story building in Juba, the capital, and that tensions grew between detainees and guards as living conditions worsened. One detainee who wanted a window open for fresh air was struck in the face by a guard, and another who complained about a lack of soap was locked in his room for days and only let out to eat, he said.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries other than their own have endured hunger, thirst and other deprivations while being detained indefinitely in places with poor human rights records and little oversight. For those expelled to South Sudan, and their families, the ordeal has come at an additional cost. Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones. Instead, the guards pocketed most of the money, families said, while detainees went for days without food or clean water, and months held incommunicado. “They used our desperate situation,” said Ngoc Phan, a U.S. citizen whose husband Tuan Phan had been detained in South Sudan for nearly a year before he was repatriated to Vietnam in June. “If that's not exploitation, I don't know what is.” It is the inevitable outcome, she said, of a U.S. immigration policy that places deportees in the custody of countries struggling with poverty and corruption, then looks the other way. Five deportees remain in custody in South Sudan, a country in East Africa where millions face severe hunger and poverty after years of civil conflict and devastating floods. The economy is in tatters, and government workers rarely receive wages. In all, Ms. Ngoc Phan said she forked over roughly $4,000 intended for food, water and a cellphone. She sent several hundred dollars on multiple occasions and each time, her husband said, guards would give him a few bananas and apples, and some peanuts. Mr. Tuan Phan, 44, said he lost 20 pounds while under confinement at a gated three-story building in Juba, the capital, and that tensions grew between detainees and guards as living conditions worsened. One detainee who wanted a window open for fresh air was struck in the face by a guard, and another who complained about a lack of soap was locked in his room for days and only let out to eat, he said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “I feared for my life every day I was there,” he said.

articles.title: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The European Union on Sunday (November 22, 2026) rejected a climate deal that omits any mention of fossil fuels , as the UN climate talks in Türkiye pushed into record extra time. Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”. “We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr. O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end. Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale. The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas. “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr. O’Brien. Ahead of the closing session, COP31 President and Türkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum had urged parties to find a compromise, after nearly two weeks of grinding negotiations led to a complete stalemate in the final moments. “We had negotiations and we listened to everyone patiently,” Mr. Kurum told the final plenary. “We wanted to give a good message to the rest of the world.” Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching political agreement to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the EU and island nations threatened by rising seas protested after a proposed text did not mention fossil fuels by name. Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petro-States such as oil-rich Saudi Arabia. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP . Threats of a walkout on Saturday (November 21, 2026) prompted Türkiye and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the EU and Saudi Arabia, but a compromise remained elusive. The latest text introduces an oblique reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels, but stops short of naming them explicitly.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The text also proposed retaining a contentious push to expand carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. Climate campaigners had urged countries to reject the deal. “This text isn’t a climate plan. It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 06:15:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The European Union on Sunday (November 22, 2026) rejected a climate deal that omits any mention of fossil fuels , as the UN climate talks in Türkiye pushed into record extra time. Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”. “We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr. O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end. Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale. The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas. “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr. O’Brien. Ahead of the closing session, COP31 President and Türkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum had urged parties to find a compromise, after nearly two weeks of grinding negotiations led to a complete stalemate in the final moments. “We had negotiations and we listened to everyone patiently,” Mr. Kurum told the final plenary. “We wanted to give a good message to the rest of the world.” Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching political agreement to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the EU and island nations threatened by rising seas protested after a proposed text did not mention fossil fuels by name. Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petro-States such as oil-rich Saudi Arabia. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP . Threats of a walkout on Saturday (November 21, 2026) prompted Türkiye and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the EU and Saudi Arabia, but a compromise remained elusive. The latest text introduces an oblique reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels, but stops short of naming them explicitly.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The text also proposed retaining a contentious push to expand carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. Climate campaigners had urged countries to reject the deal. “This text isn’t a climate plan. It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Geopolitical (Adjective)
भू-राजनैतिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Geopolitical' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Frustration (Noun)
निराशा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Frustration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Contentious (Adjective)
विवादास्पद — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Contentious' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN..." (Hinglish Arth: आयरलैंड के जलवायु और ऊर्जा मंत्री दारागह ओ'ब्रायन ने कहा कि यूरोपीय संघ अंताल्या संधि का समर्थन नहीं करेगा, जिसमें "जीवाश्म ईंधन का भी उल्लेख नहीं है", क्योंकि संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु वार्ता रिकॉर्ड अतिरिक्त समय में चली गई।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org." (Hinglish Arth: पर्यावरण समूह 350.org की सारा शॉ ने कहा, "यह प्रदूषण फैलाते रहने का लाइसेंस है।")
